sam: quick heads-up — ran a fused-attn sweep with epilogue+qkvpack AND paged-KV turned on (T4 cluster). seeing a regression for long seqs.

sam: short summary: baseline (epilogue=false,qkvpack=false,pagedkv=false) = 11.8ms @ seq=1024, bsz=1. with epilogue+qkvpack+pagedkv = 15.9ms (+35%). reproducible locally and in ci.

maria: ouch. do you have the profiler hotspots or the nvprof/nsight command you used?

sam: use this to reproduce/prof:
```
# run from infra/bench
./run_attn_bench --model=gpt-small --seq_len=1024 --batch=1 \
  --flags epilogue=true,qkvpack=true,pagedkv=true --device=t4 --iters=50
# then nvprof/rocprof capture
nvprof --metrics gld_efficiency,gst_efficiency -o prof.nvvp ./run_attn_bench ...
```

sam: top-line from the sampling profiler (summed across iteration windows):
```
fused_attn_epilogue_kernel  42%
softmax_kernel             18%
kv_page_loads              12%
kv_cache_writeback         9%
memcpy / prefetch logic    7%
other kernels              12%
```

kevin: interesting — the extra ~4ms looks like L2/L3 pressure from the epilogue writing into the paged KV region. i tried toggling prefetch distance and that changed numbers. with prefetch_distance=2 we get ~12.6ms, with =4 we go back to ~15ms.

olivia: that matches my hypothesis: when epilogue fusion writes combined (bias+rope) results into the KV pages you get eviction of hot Q/K/V tiles. paged-kv causes more strided accesses and hurts cache residency. epilogue fusion saves some compute but trades off worse memory locality for large seqs.

maria: any quick workaround to avoid rolling back the whole fusion? maybe conditional in kernel chooser: disable epilogue fusion when pagedkv=true && seq_len>=512 && head_dim<=64?

kevin: yeah, a kernel-chooser guard is lowest-risk. simple heuristic I tested: if pagedkv && seq>=512 && (qkv_pack_enabled) then prefer non-epilogue variant. result: 12.1ms. also added a soft fallback to allow forced-epilogue via env for testing.

perf-bot: ci-bench summary: benchmark/attn/2287654321 delta +32% for fused-epilogue combo on t4-prod. full artifact: ci-artifacts/attn/2287654321/report.html

ci-bot: created perf/regression/3124 — "epilogue fusion causes L2 thrash with paged-KV & qkvpack on long seqs". assigned_to: kevin, sam. link: https://go.re/redwood/perf/3124

olivia: notes for the fix:
- implement kernel-chooser guard described above (kevin already prototyped)
- add telemetry: count fallback hits per model+seq bin, emit SLO tag so we can monitor client impact
- add microbench in ci for seq={256,512,1024} bsz={1,2} with pagedkv toggles

sam: i'll push the prototype change to kevin's branch, add perf-run and the telemetry, and request a small canary rollout to dedicated. if numbers stay <= baseline we'll keep the optimized epilogue path on by default; otherwise kernel-chooser stays conservative.

maria: sounds good. documented repro steps and perf numbers in the issue. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: leaving a note — longer-term we should explore writing epilogue outputs into a staging buffer + async flush to paged-kv to avoid eviction, but that's more invasive. filing follow-up techdebt after the guard lands.

sam: action items -> perf/regression/3124 (kevin/sam), add ci microbench + telemetry (sam), short canary (kevin). closing thread here but ping me if you want to see the nvprof output/raw traces.
